entries.title: Montana Senate map shows two of the candidates on the ballot
entries.wrong: The page maps Seth Bodnar (independent) and Kurt Alme (Republican) only. It leaves out Democrat Alani Bankhead, Libertarian Kyle Austin and one write-in candidate. The headline share is therefore a share of the two shown candidates' votes, not of all votes.
entries.done: Added a dated note at the top of the page that names the omitted candidates and says what the shares mean. The map data is unchanged. A full four-candidate version is planned.
entries.prevent: Every race must list its full ballot, and any omitted candidate must appear in a page note. A check for this is being built.

entries.title: Thirty-seven more pages map only some of the candidates on the ballot
entries.wrong: According to The Green Papers or Ballotpedia, these pages show two candidates while more were on the ballot. Senate: AR, CO, FL, IA, ID, IL, KY, MI, MN, MS, NC, NE, NJ, OK, OR, SC, TN, TX. Governor: WY, AR, AZ, CO, FL, ID, IL, MI, MN, NE, NV, OH, OK, OR, PA, SC, TN, WI. House: ND. Shares on these pages are shares of the two shown candidates, not of all votes. California (top-two), Alabama, Georgia, Kansas, New Mexico, New York (including the two New York City pages), Louisiana, Iowa governor, Wyoming Senate and the South Dakota races are complete. All 54 pages have now been checked.
entries.done: Added a dated note with the count, names where known, and a source link to each audited page. Map data is unchanged. The audit continues; each result is added here.

entries.found_by: editor review while building the ballot card
entries.title: The "Votes cast" bar counted only the two shown candidates
entries.wrong: The bar labelled "Votes cast" used the sum of the two shown candidates' votes as its total, so it read as a share of all votes cast. On 53 pages that is not what it measures.
entries.done: Relabelled the bar "Votes for the two shown" on 53 pages. California, a top-two race, keeps "Votes cast". Every page now also has an "On the ballot" card with the candidate count. Numbers are unchanged.
entries.prevent: A label that says "votes cast" or "of the vote" must match its denominator. A check for this wording is planned.

entries.title: Nebraska Senate: ballot count corrected from five to three
entries.wrong: Our note and card said two of five candidates were on the ballot. A July Ballotpedia report listed three on the ballot after the Democratic nominee withdrew. A later Ballotpedia headline counts five names.
entries.done: The page now says three candidates and names Mike Marvin as not shown. It says the count is being confirmed. Map data is unchanged. Superseded by E-2026-006: five candidates were on the ballot.
entries.prevent: A roster with conflicting sources shows the lower confirmed count and a caveat until a certified list settles it.

entries.title: Georgia and South Carolina Senate: ballot counts were too high
entries.wrong: Our notes said 7 candidates were on the ballot in Georgia and 10 in South Carolina. Both counts came from Ballotpedia and included people who were not on the general election ballot. The Green Papers lists 2 for Georgia (Ossoff and Collins, plus 3 write-ins) and 4 for South Carolina (Andrews, Graham, Whitener and Hackett). The South Carolina vote shares add up to 100% across those four plus write-ins, so no other name was on the ballot. Georgia is now complete on our map.
entries.done: Both notes now show the corrected count and the source. Map data is unchanged.
entries.prevent: When two sources disagree, the higher-ranked source wins and the other is logged. A state election office list will replace these when we can read one.

entries.title: Nebraska Senate: ballot count corrected again, from three to five
entries.wrong: E-2026-004 said three candidates were on the ballot. Five were: Ricketts, Osborn, Robin Richards, Mike Marvin and Chuck Conboy. Marvin suspended his campaign but stayed on the ballot. The Nebraska Examiner and The Green Papers both report five.
entries.done: The note and card now say five and name the three candidates not shown. Map data is unchanged.
entries.prevent: A candidate who suspends a campaign is counted if the state left the name on the ballot. We confirm this against a second source before lowering a count.

entries.found_by: audit against the state election office
entries.title: Wisconsin governor: the ballot count was too high
entries.wrong: Our note said 3 candidates were on the Wisconsin governor ballot. That count came from Ballotpedia and included a registered write-in. The Wisconsin Elections Commission's Candidates on Ballot list shows 2: Tiffany (Republican) and Crowley (Democratic). Both are on our map, so the map is complete.
entries.done: The note now shows 2 and cites the Wisconsin Elections Commission. Map data is unchanged.
entries.prevent: Write-ins are never counted as ballot candidates. The state election office list outranks other sources, and any disagreement is logged.

entries.found_by: audit against the state election office
entries.title: Texas and North Carolina Senate: ballot counts were too high
entries.wrong: Our notes said 7 candidates were on the Texas Senate ballot and 5 in North Carolina. Both counts came from Ballotpedia. The Texas Secretary of State lists 3 on the ballot (Paxton, Talarico and Brown); the other 4 names were certified write-ins. The North Carolina State Board of Elections lists 4 (Cooper, Whatley, Bray and Dublin); two names in our count were not on its list.
entries.done: Both notes now show the corrected count and cite the state office. Map data is unchanged.
entries.prevent: Write-ins are never counted as ballot candidates. The state election office list outranks other sources, and any disagreement is logged.

banners.note: per_entry: a page shows a banner only if an entry on it sets banner true, or is S1 and not corrected. all: every page with a roster gap shows one.

log.text: Page banners for roster gaps were removed. Every page still shows the "On the ballot" card with the full count, and each gap is still listed here. Banners return for any entry that sets banner or is S1 and open.
